correctness.rationale: Original v1 nearest-neighbor median on the three-path is exactly the sign-controlled affine map; derivation and contraction proof cover all 0<s<1, ties and parameter boundaries. For s≤2/3 exterior flips decrease amplitude until an invariant sign branch; for s>2/3 a constant sign forces an eventual exact repelling fixed point, yielding countably many exceptional starts. At s=3/4 both branches of [-3,3] cover it with slope -2, so the full Bernoulli itinerary holds for uniform normalized starts. The saved verifier checks 7,776 rational updates, 1,022 cylinder lengths, 372 trajectories and 20 witness steps; experiments are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The original v1 source supplies the synchronous neighbor-valued model, simulations and mean-field approximations but no path switching classification. The 2025 v3 changed its median definition and hence does not dominate the v1-specific result. Earlier asynchronous median consensus results do not imply the exact original-rule itinerary. Six actual published-finding corpus searches and targeted literature searches returned no matching model-specific theorem; classical affine-map Bernoulli coding is credited as prior, not claimed original. A residual unindexed-priority possibility remains.
residual_risks: The 2024 original source contains awkward formula rendering; its explicit discrete-neighbor candidate set and nearest-choice convention are used, not the revised 2025 real-minimizer rule.
Earlier asynchronous model full text and possible later unpublished or unindexed statements may include equivalent conclusions; no independent priority certification.
The Bernoulli coding is standard for full-branch maps; its originality is only the exact reduction of this original opinion mechanism and parameter-specific realization.

value.rationale: On the smallest connected graph with two eligible median neighbors, there is a sharp qualitative transition at s=2/3 between influence-choice stabilization and indefinitely fluctuating influence decisions, even though scalar opinions always converge. The full Bernoulli itinerary at s=3/4 exhibits maximal symbolic unpredictability from a deterministic social update and randomly sampled initial conditions. The candidate is a motivated structural boundary and not an arbitrary invariant or routine subcase.
